newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Feb housing completions rose 10.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Feb housing completions rose 10.8 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:
The department said the 1.505 million unit annual rate in February housing completions was the highest since an annualized rate of 1.508 million units in January 1990.

Commerce said February completions of single-family homes rose 9.3 percent after a revised 6.0 percent drop in January and a revised 2.3 percent increase in December. Previously, the department said single-family completions fell 7.4 percent in January and increased 1.4 percent in December.

February multi-family unit completions rose 17.5 percent after a revised 17.9 percent drop in January and a revised 9.6 percent increase in December. Previously, the department said January multi-family unit completions fell 19.5 percent and that December multi-family unit completions were up 7.9 percent.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis rose in February to 99,400 units from 95,400 units in January but fell from 141,800 units in December. In February 1996, actual completions were reported at 91,000.

Privately-owned housing units under construction rose to a seasonally adjusted 829,000 in February from 818,000 in January and 815,000 in December. They compare with 798,000 units under construction in February 1996.
